questions.question: Which project–contributor pairings at the AAIF founding are correct? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: The founding contributions were Anthropic's MCP, Block's goose, and OpenAI's AGENTS.md (plus agentgateway). Google is a platinum member but didn't contribute goose.

questions.question: Which statements about the AAIF are true? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: It operates under the Linux Foundation
It is a vendor-neutral home where no single company dominates
Launch platinum members included AWS, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI alongside Anthropic and Block
The AAIF was founded by a single company and later opened to others

questions.explanation: All four facts come from the founding announcement — a legitimate 'All of the above'.

questions.question: Which are host applications in the MCP ecosystem? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Hosts are AI applications that coordinate MCP clients — Claude Desktop, goose, and MCP-enabled IDEs qualify. The Registry is discovery infrastructure, not a host.

questions.question: Which benefits does neutral foundation governance give the MCP ecosystem? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Competing vendors (AWS, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI) can all invest in one standard no rival controls
Downstream developers are protected from unilateral pricing/compatibility/deprecation decisions
Evolution happens by community consensus via SEPs and Working Groups
It guarantees every MCP server is free of vulnerabilities

questions.explanation: Governance neutrality delivers cooperation, protection from unilateral change, and consensus-driven evolution — it does not (and cannot) guarantee implementation security.
